target_claim: The solution's transformation (copy the 3m integers of a 3Partition instance S, append 9m elements each equal to 0, set n = m) is an answer-preserving polynomial-time reduction 3Partition <=_p 12Partition; in particular (lines 0029-0034) 'each Ai must contain exactly 3 non-zero elements (because 3m non-zero elements distributed into m subsets requires 3 per subset) and 9 zeros', so any 12Partition solution of S' yields a 3Partition solution of S.
failing_input: S = [3, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1] (m = 2, |S| = 6 <= 12, 3Partition target T = 6). Constructed instance S' = [3,3,3,1,1,1] ++ [0]*18, n = 2, |S'| = 24. Smallest lexicographic witness in the exhaustive sweep: S = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3] (T = 4). 18 of the 210 multisets of 6 positive integers with values in 1..5 fail.
observed_vs_claimed: Claimed: 12Partition(S') = YES iff 3Partition(S) = YES. Observed on S = [3,3,3,1,1,1]: brute-force oracle gives 3Partition(S) = NO (no 3-element subset sums to 6: 1+1+1=3, 3+1+1=5, 3+3+1=7, 3+3+3=9), while exhaustive enumeration over ALL C(23,11) = 1,352,078 ways to split the 24 elements of S' into two 12-element blocks gives 12Partition(S') = YES, witnessed by A1 = {3,3} + ten 0s (sum 6, 12 elements) and A2 = {3,1,1,1} + eight 0s (sum 6, 12 elements). The non-zero counts per block are 2 and 4, not 3 and 3, so the forcing claim on lines 0031-0032 is false: the size-12 constraint is satisfied by padding zeros, and nothing forces the non-zero elements to be split 3-per-block. The reduction therefore maps a NO instance of 3Partition to a YES instance of 12Partition and is not answer-preserving. The same mismatch is reproduced on the second triage adversarial input S = [2,2,2,3,3,6] (oracle NO, reduction YES via {6,3} and {2,2,2,3}) and on 18/210 instances of the exhaustive family.
faithfulness_notes: The transformation is implemented verbatim from lines 0010-0017: S' = list(S) + [0]*9m with n = m, giving |S'| = 12m. Because the solution asserts an 'iff', the reduction used as a decision procedure outputs 12Partition(S'); that is the implementation output compared against the oracle. Oracles use exact integer arithmetic only (no floats): oracle_3partition exhaustively enumerates all triple-partitions with equal sums; oracle_kpartition is a complete backtracking search over partitions into n blocks of exactly 12 elements with equal sums, symmetry-broken only over blocks that are currently indistinguishable in (running sum, running count). That backtracking oracle was cross-validated against a literally exhaustive C(23,11) subset enumeration on 8 constructed 24-element instances (all agree), and the reported witness is exhibited by the literal enumerator. One faithfulness caveat, recorded but NOT load-bearing for the counterexample: the solution pads with elements equal to 0, which are not positive integers as the 12Partition problem statement requires; the implementation keeps the zeros exactly as written rather than silently repairing them. The counterexample does not depend on that defect -- it depends only on the fact that equal 12-element block sums do not force equal non-zero counts. Search was exhaustive over all 210 multisets of 3m = 6 positive integers with values in 1..5 (m = 2) plus the two adversarial constructions from the triage sketches; the run is deterministic with no sampling.
